getter_and_return_cut.control_flow_premise: Bounded source CFG treats linked JAL/JALR callees as ordinary returning calls. There are only two JR RA returns and no tail J/JR-table exits. Encoded branches enter epilogues only at their gates, never after them. Blocking those two gates cuts all encoded normal returns; nonlocal exits/cancellation are outside this proof.
getter_and_return_cut.after_unpin: After successful unlock the private replay and native epilogue perform only stack loads, result transfer and return. Old-pair retirement may begin while these stack-only instructions finish. Protocol errors instead use a private epilogue copy, V0=-1 and V1=diagnostic, without retrying unpin or releasing an uncertain result.

selected_service_ownership.limits: Fresh allocation and copied backing depend on the pinned class/method globals, ordinary allocator/string imports and valid owned inputs. Field-parser bindings, arbitrary callbacks, hidden aliases and universal transitive ownership are not established here. selected_final_disposal_evidence.scope: Selected final disposal runs after the worker-stop call returns, before remaining native context teardown. selected_final_disposal_evidence.fault_boundary: Raw errors retain binding and abort through the private native epilogue without guessed unlock, repeated release, free/reset or finish. READY checks suppress the next guarded callback after a fault is observed, including after disposal and final-free unlocks; they do not make arbitrary concurrent faults atomic or stop every intervening native callback. Detached unreleased objects can leak.

local_queue_transport_review.status: Read-only native transport review and local diagnostic regressions. No queue runtime fix, firmware image, deployment or device test is introduced by this stage.
local_queue_transport_review.scope: The selected ring at absolute B89250 is followed from native POST 454B40 through WRITE 4504E0 and worker 454380/READ 450600 to init 4554E0 and shutdown 4556E0. Encoded direct callers and pinned bodies are a local source census; computed callers, scheduler behavior and external library lifetime are not closed.

record_words: argument; command zero is locally repurposed as captured session generation
transport.serial_contract: POST copies two stack words into a separately allocated eight-byte record. Successful READ copies eight bytes into worker SP+828, releases the record, clears its pointer slot and advances the read index. The worker then copies those two words into SP+820/+824 before dispatch. Records contain no retained session pointer. Native WRITE/READ return zero on success and -1 for NULL or full/empty, respectively.
transport.limits: The busy counter is read, waited on and changed with plain LW/SW. These selected bodies contain no LL/SC admission or checked raw mutex operation. Polling a zero counter followed by increment is not one atomic acquisition. WRITE does not reject an allocation NULL before its memcpy, and READ copies the requested byte count without per-record length metadata.

creation_and_start.source_contract: Init first clears all 352 context bytes, creates context+18 through 466D60, creates the ring through 450460(50), and publishes the returned pointer at 45559C before creating context+8/+C. The ring constructor allocates (capacity+5)*4 bytes and initializes its capacity, indices and busy counter. The capacity-50 ring allocation is checked for NULL.
creation_and_start.partial_failure: The ring and later mutex allocation failure branches call cleanup, but cleanup does not clear the published ring or destroyed mutex pointer slots. Pool allocations assigned to context+3C/+154 log NULL and still continue to the thread-start block. These observations do not establish a valid later use of absent pools.
creation_and_start.handshake: Startup locks context+8, calls 466BA0 with worker 454380, stores its returned word in context+4, and locks context+8 again without testing that word. Worker first locks context+C and then unlocks context+8. With successful library operations this orders worker acquisition of the lifetime mutex before startup returns. The constructor-to-worker cross-thread unlock of context+8 is the native handshake, not a portable mutex ownership proof.
creation_and_start.thread_wrapper: 466BA0 requests detached state 1 and stack size 0x20000, then calls pthread_create with an output word at its SP+3C. It does not branch on pthread_create status; it calls pthread_attr_destroy and returns that output word, which was not initialized locally before pthread_create. A thread-creation refusal can therefore leave startup waiting on its already-locked +8 with no worker to perform the intended unlock, if the raw lock blocks normally.
creation_and_start.caller_result: The only identified direct init caller at 4754F0 proceeds to another call without checking V0. A ring-allocation failure with successful cleanup can also return zero through the masked destroy facade; zero does not certify that the worker exists.

stop_and_destruction.normal_sequence: Shutdown stores stop=1 at context+10. With nonzero context+C it locks, unlocks and destroys that mutex, then frees context pools and context+14, drains/frees the ring, and destroys context+18. Worker checks stop before dequeue and after each completed dispatch/sleep; on exit it unlocks context+C at 454500. After that call its selected tail contains only saved-register loads, return and stack restoration. This is a completion-mutex convention, with a detached worker rather than a native join in the selected path.
stop_and_destruction.lifetime_limit: Native POST does not read stop or acquire context+C/+18. Shutdown has no producer admission seal or producer pin. After 4507E0 frees the ring, 4556E0 does not zero B89250; its destroyed +C/+18 slots also remain nonzero. A future init clears the context, which is not protection for an already-loaded pointer or a producer concurrent with destruction. A second uncoordinated native shutdown would again use destroyed pointers; reachability through all higher-level gates is not claimed.
stop_and_destruction.destroy_limit: 4507E0 polls the ring busy counter, then drains and frees without incrementing or otherwise claiming that counter. A writer can enter after its zero observation unless another lifetime protocol excludes that schedule. It releases unread records by pointer and advances read index; it does not execute queued command semantics. Drain-only 450720 keeps the ring allocation and also releases records without dispatch; its sole identified direct caller 42CD6C uses another global ring, not B89250.
stop_and_destruction.blocking_limit: Shutdown cannot make progress until the worker reaches its stop check and unlock. No cancellation of a stalled opaque worker service is established. If a raw lock/unlock/destroy operation fails, native facade zero does not certify worker completion or successful destruction.

masked_library_facades.mutex: 466D60 allocates 24 bytes, invokes pthread_mutex_init even for allocation NULL, and returns the saved pointer instead of init status. 466DA0/466DC0 overwrite raw lock/unlock results with zero. 466DE0 ignores destroy status, frees a nonzero pointer and returns zero. Native callers cannot treat these zero values as checked raw-operation certificates.
masked_library_facades.semaphore_scope: The selected Tidal transport/start/stop bodies above use mutex facades, not semaphore admission. Separately audited semaphore facades 466C80/466CE0/466D00/466D20 mask sem_init/wait/post/destroy results: init returns the allocation pointer after ignoring init status, wait/post return zero, destroy frees its pointer regardless of raw status. They do not supply a missing ring lifetime guarantee.
masked_library_facades.imports_resolution: .rel.plt R_MIPS_JUMP_SLOT symbol names in the pinned ELF identify the following PLT/GOT bindings; external implementation, scheduling, failure behavior and object liveness remain premises.

post_result_propagation.scope: All 13 native local continuations overwrite V0 or call another function before testing enqueue status. In particular, 4D504C and 4D5080 replace V0 with S0 before their local returns. This is not universal transitive caller handling. At 478254 and 50829C a separate status setter arms command zero as pending before POST. Native full/NULL queue rejection does not reset that status;5082B8 still calls the QR factory. The current QR-specific local POST bridge preserves the queued generation, but does not repair native queue failures or roll back preparation.

conditional_schedules.result: One admitted serial POST produces command 0/generation 1, READ copies both words and frees exactly one packet. A second READ reports empty. This is the bounded ordinary baseline.

conditional_schedules.case: full or absent queue after pending was armed
conditional_schedules.result: POST returns -1 without packet allocation; separately armed status remains1 and sidecar remains READY. This alone does not prove an indefinite UI wait.
The native path reaches memcpy(NULL, source, 8) at 450578. The diagnostic service stops there; the busy counter remains 1 and write index has not advanced. Actual libc fault/recovery is not emulated.

conditional_schedules.schedule: Pause both after busy observation at 45052C. Run each to 450550 so both retain next index 1 and busy becomes 2. Complete A, then B.
conditional_schedules.result: Both return 0 with ring read 0/write 1/busy 0. Packet A occupies slot 0 and B slot 1, but only A is logically reachable before READ reports empty. The generation mutex was released before native WRITE and WRITER remains 0. Actual concurrent invocation on the player is not asserted.

conditional_schedules.schedule: Both pass busy observation before 450644 and capture the same record pointer before 450670. Complete first READ/free, then resume second memcpy.
conditional_schedules.result: The second copy uses a record whose free has returned. This is conditional on a second concurrent consumer; only the selected Tidal worker 454380→454410 has been identified for B89250. A second stock Tidal consumer is not established.

conditional_schedules.schedule: Finish actual generic generation admission to POST+8. The actual base close gate enters CLOSING with WRITER 0/BORROWS 0. Execute the selected native drain/destroy suffix under its worker-stop premise, then resume POST.
conditional_schedules.result: B89250 still points to retired ring storage and native WRITE first reads its +C. This is a concrete allowed local cut, not full worker-stop, scheduler or shutdown emulation. Session generation protects request identity, not ring lifetime.

Source-only: if pthread_create refuses and no worker is created, the unchecked second startup lock has no intended worker unlock. If init/lock/unlock/destroy fails, masked facade results do not establish initialized objects, ownership, completion or destruction. These raw failures were not observed on a device and are not covered by the seven dynamic queue diagnostics.

remaining_obligations: Close native queue admission and drain already-admitted producers before destroy, including producers past the generation mutex and nonzero-command bypasses; establish exclusive WRITE/READ admission separately.
Seal new queue admission before destruction and wait for already-admitted users; clearing the global alone cannot protect a previously loaded ring pointer.
Handle allocation NULL and preserve explicit enqueue failure separately from prior pending-status/UI changes.

Do not hold the session mutex blindly across the native ring busy-poll wait or other unbounded queue operations. A bounded producer lease and separate checked queue synchronization need their own progress and failure contracts.
Check raw startup/stop synchronization and thread-creation outcomes before treating lifecycle completion as established. Keep external callback, allocator and library contracts explicit.
No runtime queue repair is enabled here. The diagnostic schedules are local counterexamples under stated concurrency/lifetime premises, not reports of observed device crashes.

caller_refusal_review.status: Diagnostic caller/source checks only. The current 44-hook runtime composer is unchanged; no queue admission, rollback or caller quarantine fix is introduced.
caller_refusal_review.source_verification: All 36 entries of NATIVE_WORDS were independently compared with the pinned source image. They cover the four command-zero producer continuations and native worker notification/stop/return suffix.

observations.result: Under CLOSING policy refusal or a preexisting FAILED raw-error state, command-zero POST returns -1 with diagnostic 116 or 22. Its caller retains command-zero pending=1 and continues through the separately forced command-six branch. The native nonzero-command bypass queues command six with argument zero and arms its own pending state. The selected caller returns zero.

Actual native COPY_INPUT 5134C0 copies the two bounded strings into global credential buffers before the guarded POST rejects CLOSING with diagnostic 116. Native continuation reads status and, when needed, rearms pending=1 before its opaque UI call. No packet is queued. This identifies a caller-local recovery obligation; the fixture does not perform account or network operations.

The fixture changes lifecycle to CLOSING after capture unlock. The QR-specific POST identity check refuses and skips construction, but the preceding RESET_FILE call, pending=1 and existing owner flag remain. No rollback of those earlier native effects is implemented. RESET_FILE is observed through a bounded service substitute, not a real file operation.

observations.case: QR native queue-full failure after successful policy admission
observations.result: With the native ring already full, policy-admitted POST returns -1 without publishing a packet. Its caller still invokes the native constructor path: a private payload receives generation 1 and the owner flag is cleared. Pending remains 1. Session policy refusal and enqueue failure therefore have different native continuation behavior.

Queued generation 2 against current generation 1 rejects before input services and before the native busy-set call. Pending remains 1, WRITER remains zero and PHASE remains READY. The helper jumps to WORK_SKIP 4544EC, bypassing the busy-clear call at 4544E4; the fixture-selected stop suffix still returns normally.

observations.case: worker END raw lock refusal after actual busy-set
observations.result: The fixture first executes successful BEGIN, including actual notification (20,1) and WRITER=1. Without changing the queued packet, it injects raw LOCK result 22 at WORK_END. PHASE becomes FAILED with INIT_ERROR=22; pending=1, WRITER=1 and the prior busy-set remain. WORK_SKIP bypasses native busy-clear, then executes the independently owned worker-mutex unlock and ordinary return. Returning from that worker suffix does not clear the failed sidecar pin or certify successful result commit.

fixture_limits: Input copy, native POST/status instructions, selected caller continuations and worker stop epilogue execute their pinned bodies. UI, configuration, credential-source, file, factory and network services use bounded substitutes where the fixture declares them; there are no real UI, file, network or device actions.

The command-six continuation is deliberately forced by the OTHER_INPUT substitute writing nonempty bounded strings. It proves the selected native branch can continue after command-zero refusal, not that a particular device account configuration does so.
The PAUSE substitute sets the native stop flag to select a bounded stop-and-return suffix. The test does not emulate a scheduler or prove real stop latency, cancellation or full shutdown.

WORKER_MUTEX is modeled as independently owned across the loop. Its native unlock facade executes, with the raw library operation supplied by a bounded substitute. This is not evidence of portable cross-thread ownership semantics or real pthread completion.
CLOSING and raw error injection are explicit local conditions. The tests show native continuation and diagnostic state under those conditions; they do not report observed failures on the player.

synchronization_obligations: Worker response publication, worker cleanup and QR destructor must share reclamation authority.
Known readers at 48CAC0, 48CE80, 4B1620 and 4B16E0 retain source fields across service or callback calls. A pointer load protected only during acquisition is insufficient.
Caller-supplied callbacks at 48CEE4/48CF5C require a reentry/progress contract before holding a non-reentrant mutex over their full use.
The two concrete upper copy/field consumers need one coherent response generation in addition to physical lifetime.
Existing worker and dialog lifetime locks are separate from a proven shared-session borrow protocol.
